First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{8}+\sqrt{2}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{8}+\sqrt{2},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{8}-\sqrt{2}} & = \\ \frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{8}-\sqrt{2}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{8}+\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{8}+\sqrt{2}} & = \\ \frac{(1+\sqrt{5})(\sqrt{8}+\sqrt{2})}{(\sqrt{8}+\sqrt{2})(\sqrt{8}-\sqrt{2})} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{8}+\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{40}+\sqrt{10}}{(\sqrt{8})^{2}-(\sqrt{2})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{2\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{2}+2\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{10}}{8-2} & = \\ \frac{3\sqrt{2}+3\sqrt{10}}{6}= \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{10}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
